INTRODUCTION 
 
 I, the Chairman of the Department related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, having been 
authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present 
this One Hundred Thirty-Eighth (138th) Report on Action Taken on One Hundred 
Twenty-Ninth (129th) Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2023-24) 
pertaining to the Department of Legal Affairs (Ministry of Law & Justice). 
2. The 1 29th Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Law and Justice was 
presented to Rajya Sabha  on the 15 th March, 2023 and laid on the Table of Lok 
Sabha on the 20th March, 2023.  
3. The Department of Legal Affairs, of the Ministry of Law & Justice furnished 
their Action Taken Replies on the 11 5th Report of the Committee on 13th October, 
2023. The Committee considered the draft 125th Report and adopted the same in its 
meeting held on 7th December, 2023. 
4. For the facility of reference and convenience, the observations and 
recommendations of the Committee have been printed in bold letters in the body of 
the Report.

R E P O R T  
 This Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by 
the Department of Legal Affairs (Ministry of Law &  Justice) on the 
recommendations / observations of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice in its One Hundred 
Twenty-Ninth (129th) Report on Demands for Grants (2023-24) pertaining to the 
Department of Legal Affairs (Ministry of Law & Justice), which was presented to 
the Rajya Sabha on the 15th March, 2023 and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on 
the 20th March, 2023. 
2. The Committee had made 19 recommendations/observations in its 1 29th 
Report. Replies of the Department thereto have been categorized and scrutinized 
under four chapters on the basis of satisfaction of the Committee. These replies 
have been categorized as follows: 
Chapter – I:  Recommendations/observations (9) which have been accepted by 
the Department, i.e. in respect of paras 2.11, 2.18, 3.12, 3.18, 3.20, 
3.24, 3.29, 3.30 and 3.35 of the Report. The Committee is pleased 
to note that the Department has accepted those recommendations. 
Chapter – II:  Recommendations/observations (2) which the Committee does not 
desire to pursue in view of the replies given by the Department, i.e. 
in respect of paras 3.10 and 3.11 of the Report. The Committee is 
satisfied with the explanations advanced by the Department and 
does not wish to pursue those as of now.  
Chapter – III:  Recommendations/observations (8) in respect of which Committee 
has not accepted the replies of the Department, i.e. with regard to 
paras 2.1 5,  3.1 9, 3.23, 3.39,3.40, 3.41, 3.42 and 3.43  of the 
Report. The Committee does not accept the reasons given by the 
Department and reiterates the same. 
3. The Committee desires that the Department should furnish pointed and 
detailed Action Taken Notes in respect of all the further 
Recommendations/Observations made by the Committee in this report. 
4. The details of the ATR have been discussed in the respective Chapters in the 
succeeding pages. For reference purpose, para numbers of the original report (i.e. 
of 1 29th Report) have been mentioned at the e nd of each 
recommendation/observation.

CHAPTER I

Overall Assessment of the Demands for Grants  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1.0 Out of the 30 Benches from which the ITAT is operating, only on 3 locations they are 
having their own building. On other 20 locations they are operating from the premises given by 
the Central Government and other Government bodies and on 7 locations from b uildings of 
private owners. Thus there is an urgent need to augment and enhance the infrastructural needs of 
the Tribunal. Accordingly, the Committee recommends the Government to provide adequate 
funds to ITAT to complete their ongoing projects on schedule . The Department should approach 
the MoF to get the funds required for the FY 2023 -24 so that the ongoing projects are not stalled 
due to scanty allocations. (2.11) 
 
Action Taken

a phased manner as the exercise is largely dependent on the availability of requisite funds for the 
same, by way of budgetary grants. As of now, t he following projec ts of ITAT are under 
construction and are required to be completed for its occupation as per timelines conveyed by the 
executing agencies. The status of the ongoing projects and the budgetary requirements are

VACANCIES OF NOTARIES 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.11 The Committee is concerned to note the level of vacancies in the central quota of public 
Notaries. More than 50% of posts are vacant and the pace of filling of vacancies is very slow. 
The Department has started providing facility for candidates to fill the application forms and to 
submit the fe e through online mode. The renewal process is also being made online. These are 
welcome steps aimed to enhance the pace of filling up of vacancies. It will also bring out 
transparency in the process. The Committee expects the Department to pick the pace of  filling of 
vacant posts of Notaries and to fill all the vacancies in a time-bound manner. (3.18) 
Action Taken 
1.12 It is submitted that efforts are being made to fill the vacancies of Notaries in different 
States/UTs in the country.  
(i)  In the month of February, 2023, 2nd list of 672 recommended candidates for appointment 
of Notaries in Gujarat has been published, on the basis of interviews conducted from 03.10.2022 
to 28.10.2022.  
(ii)  Further, Notary Cell has conducted online interviews for 4781 applicants for appointment 
of Central Public Notaries in the State of Karnataka in February, 2023.  
(iii)  Besides this, interviews have been conducted on 29.03.2023 for 103 candidates for 
appointment of Notaries in seven North -Eastern States (i.e. Meghalaya, A runachal Pradesh, 
Sikkim, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland and Mizoram) and the result has been uploaded for 59 
recommended candidates on Department‟s official website on 04.04.2023.  
(iv)  The Government plans to fill the vacancies in a phased manner as per the  vacancies in

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS 
ON EMPANELMENT OF ADVOCATES FOR UNION OF INDIA 
 
Q.1 What is ‘Panel Counsel’ for Union of India? 
Department of Legal Affairs has been mandated with conduct of litigations on behalf of 
Union of India before various courts / tribunals in India . For this purpose, Department of 
Legal Affairs empanels Advocates for various courts / tribunals in the country generally 
for a period of three years or until further orders, whichever is earlier. There are several 
categories (court -wise) in which this De partment empanels Advocates and such 
empanelled Advocates are collectively called as „Panel Counsel‟ for Union of India.  
However, „Panel Counsel‟ is not a civil post and as such they are not regular Government 
Servant.  
 
Q.2 Documentation/details required in the application for empanelment as a Panel 
Counsel for Union of India? 
 (a)   Name of court / tribunal seeking empanelment for. 
(b) Desired category of Panel Counsel available in that court /  
tribunal.  
(c) Certification on part of willing Advocate that he/she will be bound by all the 
terms & conditions (including fee) applicable to desired category of „Panel 
Counsel‟ in the desired court/tribunal. 
(d) A detailed and duly signed Bio -data may be enclosed with application 
incorporating the necessary details lik e name, postal address, contact numbers, 
email, legal qualifications, full enrollment number with the Bar Council 
concerned.

Q.4 What emoluments are paid to ‘Panel Counsel’? 
 
As „Panel Counsel‟ for Union of India are not Government Servant, they are not paid 
salaries and allowances. They are paid professional fee on case to case basis in lieu of 
their services as per the fee schedule applicable to their panel category. However,  there 
are a few categories of „Panel Counsel‟ which are paid retainership fee on monthly basis 
throughout their term in the entitled category. The fee schedule in this regard is as per 
this Department‟s OM No. 26(1)/2014-Judl. dated 01.10.2015 to be read with other OMs 
containing detailed terms & conditions applicable to „Panel Counsel‟. 
 

 
15 
 
 
Q.5 What is procedure for allotment of cases to ‘Panel Counsel’? 
  
Except in the Supreme Court of India, in all other courts / tribunals, allotment of cases to 
Panel Counsel is made by the Litigation In -charge of court concerned. The Litigation In -
charges have  been decided by the Department of Legal Affairs in OM No. J -
12017/1/2019-Judicial dated 21.10.2019. While in Supreme Court, Ld. Attorney General 
for India selects cases for his own  appearance while other cases are marked by the Ld. 
Solicitor General of India to Additional Solicitors General of India and Panel Counsel 
vide OM No. J-12017/1/2022-Judicial dated 13.09.2022.  
 
Q.6 Is there any sanctioned strength of Panel Counsel (Court-wise)? 
As stated earlier „Panel Counsel‟ for Union of India is not a civil post hence, the concept 
of sanctioned strength is not applicable in case of „Panel Counsel‟. Advocates a re 
empanelled for a particular court / tribunal by Department of Legal Affairs in numbers as 
required from time to time.   
 
Q.7 Are the Panel Counsel for Union of India allowed for private practice? 
Panel Counsel for Union of India may continue their private practice but with restriction 
to the extent that they cannot appear / advise in matters against Union of India in any 
manner vide Department of Legal Affairs OM No. J -16/11/2017-Judicial dated 
08.02.2018.

INCOME TAX APPELLATE TRIBUNAL (ITAT) 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.17 From the information regarding vacancies in the ITAT, as provided by the Department it 
may be seen that about 40% of posts of Member (Accountant) and 29% of posts of Member 
(Judicial) is lying vacant. However, the Law Secretary has informed the Committee that the 
process of filling up of vacancies are underway in accordance with the provisions of the Tribunal 
Reforms Act and all the vacancies are expected to be filled up by March, 2023. The Comm ittee, 
therefore, is appreciative of the efforts of the Department in this regard and it hopes that the 
vacancies are filled up as per the timeline indicated by the Law Secretary. (3.29) 
1.18 Further, as regard pendency of appeals at the ITAT, it may be se en that from 2018 -19 
when the pendency was 92,205 it has substantially reduced to 37,118 in the year 2022 -23. The 
Department has informed that this marked decline in the pendency is primarily because of the 
fact that a large number of cases are now being s ettled through “Vivad se Vishwas Scheme” (No 
Dispute but Trust Scheme) of the Income -Tax Department. The Committee takes note of the 
reduction institution of appeals to the Tribunal due to implementation of the "Vivad se Vishwas 
Scheme" and appreciates the  efforts of the Government in this regard. With institution of the 
appeals going downwards and all the vacant positions in the Tribunal are filled, the Committee 
expects to see a very low/no pendency from the next year. (3.30) 
 
 

 
17 
Action Taken 
 
1.19 In the year of 2021-22, the Department of Legal Affairs has filled up the vacant posts viz. 
12 posts of Judicial Members and 09 posts of Accountant Members in the Income Tax Appellate 
Tribunal. The Department of Legal Affairs, in the month of September, 2022, has issued fresh 
vacancy circular to fill up the 18 posts of Judicial Members and 22 posts of Accountant Members 
in the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. The process of selection of candidates for Members 
(Judicial /Accountant) has made substantial progress and t he interaction process with applicants 
has been concluded and the Search-cum-Selection Committee (SCSC) under the Chairpersonship 
of a sitting Judge of the Hon'ble Supreme Court has submitted a list of recommended candidates 
for the consideration of the Government and further appropriate action.  
 
1.20 Also the 'Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme' is doing well to reduce the number of pending cases 
in ITAT. The Central Government's efforts to fill up the existing vacancy in ITAT during the 
current year, will further facilitate in reducing the pending cases of ITAT in the next few years.  
 
INDIA INTERNATIONAL ARBITRATION CENTRE (IIAC) 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.21 With the operationalization of the IIAC the Committee expects the Centre to strive and 
achieve the vision with which it has been created i.e. to strengthen an independent & 
autonomous arbitration regime; to compete with other reputed international arbitration centres; to 
arbitrate on big ticket infrastructure projects disputes involving Central or State Governments, 
PSUs a parties or PPP projects; and to aid in effort in making India a hub of international 
commercial arbitration. In this endeavour, the Comm ittee expects the Government and 
Department of Legal Affairs, in particular, to whole heartedly support the Centre. (3.35) 
 
Action Taken 
 
1.22 The Centre aims to implement advanced technology in order to offer a completely digital, 
paperless experience for all stakeholders. From registering arbitrators to managing the entire 
arbitration process, everything is proposed to be done digitally, making  the process more 
transparent, efficient and accessible globally. Necessary steps are being taken for development of 
the process/web and software application by the Centre.   
  
1.23 Further, considering requirements of an Arbitration Centre of international standards, the 
Centre is being considered to be re -designed/revamped and requisite action in this regard has 
also been initiated. 
  
1.24 The Centre has signed a MoU with IIM Rohtak to undertake collaborative activities to 
develop awareness and promotion campaigns that will align the goal of creating awareness in the 
field of arbitration and making India an international hub for arbitration. 
  

 
18 
1.25 The IIAC has finalized and notified various regulations for making it operational and 
fully funct ional. The Department is in the process of writing to all the Government 
Ministries/Departments and CPSEs that IIAC may be earmarked as the designated arbitral 
institution to facilitate resolution of the disputes pertaining to them with private parties etc ., 
wherever the option of Arbitration is to be taken recourse to. 
  
1.26 The Department of Legal Affairs is committed towards providing all requisite support to 
the Centre, in order to enable it to achieve its objectives.

CHAPTER II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE 
DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES GIVEN BY 
THE DEPARTMENT 
STAFF STRENGTH IN THE DEPARTMENT 
 
Recommendation/observation  
 
2.0 The Department of Legal Affairs has been functioning with about 50% of the sanctioned 
strength for quite a long time, across its grades. The Department has admitted that the shortage of 
manpower for such long duration is affecting their smooth functioning. The Committee has been 
for long; in almost every DFG reports, is recommending the Dep artment to take remedial actions 
to get rid of this perennial shortage of manpower in the Department. (3.10) 
2.1 The ILS, which is the mainstay of the Department and whose cadre control rests with the 
Department itself, has a vacancy of above 50%. The Depa rtment has further informed that they 
have initiated reforming the RRs of the cadre and vacancies will be filled thereafter. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to complete the revision of the RRs, at the 
earliest and start filling up of th e vacant position in a dedicated manner. Further, the RRs should 
be revised in such a way so as to avoid possibility of future litigations, as litigations have been 
one of the reasons for vacancies remaining unfilled. The eligibility conditions and career 
prospects in the ILS should be framed in such a manner, that it attracts the best and the brightest 
candidates from the market. (3.11) 
 
Action Taken 
 
2.2 Indian Legal Service (ILS) is an organized Group -A Service, which is governed by the 
Indian Legal Serv ice Rules, 1957. A cadre review of this service is under process, which is the 
first cadre review since this service came into being in 1957. 
 
2.3        In its various meetings, the Cadre Review Committee (CRC) of the Department of 
Personnel & Training di scussed proposals of Department of Legal Affairs, which include 
improving flexibility in allocation of Indian Legal Service (ILS) officers to various Ministries 
and Departments, issue related to provision of reserves in the ILS cadre, merger of the cadre o f 
ILS to facilitate requirement based horizontal mobility and career progression, creation of posts 
above the SAG level, change in existing sanctioned strength (cadre wise) of ILS cadre as well as 
change in method of recruitment in ILS cadre. This cadre re view will help in mitigating potential 
legal disputes in the service as well as enhancing the overall efficiency and fairness of the 
recruitment process of ILS cadre. 
 
2.4.         These recommendations of CRC is under consideration of the Government and is 
expected to be finalized shortly. 
 

 
20 
CHAPTER III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE 
COMMITTEE DOES NOT ACCEPT THE REASONS GIVEN BY THE 
DEPARTMENT AND REITERATES ITS RECOMMENDATIONS 
Overall Assessment of the Demands for Grants 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.0 From the submission of the Institute and analysis of the functioning of the ILI over the 
years, the Committee is constrained to observe that a premier institution founded for promoting 
and conducting legal research is becomin g insignificant day-by-day due to lack of funding from 
the Government. Faculty positions are remaining vacant, basic renovation and upkeep of the 
institution are held up due to lack of funds. Only a skeletal faculty/staff are maintained with the 
limited grants provided by the Government. As we don't have many institutions in the country 
for legal research and thus, the Government should maintain this institution and not let it die a 
slow death. The Committee wants to see the Institute to become a centre of excellence in the 
field of legal research, for which it requires the support of the Government. However, the 
Committee feels that if the Government is not in a position to maintain this institute, it is better 
to hand it over to some other institutions like Supreme Court of India or BCI etc., like they did in 
case of Institute of Constitutional & Parliamentary Studies (ICPS) which was handed over to the 
Lok Sabha Secretariat. (2.15) 
Action Taken  
3.1 The Department of Legal Affairs provides recurring Grants -in-Aid to the Indian Law 
Institute (ILI) for salary and general purposes. The Department also provides Grants -in-Aid to 
ILI for special purpose, whenever it was required. The Department released Rs. 6.50 crore to ILI 
as special Grants-in-Aid for payment of property tax in the Financial Year 2021 -22 and Rs.1.00 
crore to ILI as additional Grants -in-Aid for payment of arrears of salary to employees of ILI on 
implementation of the recommendations of the 7 th CPC in the Financial Year 2018 -19. The 
Department has also increased the Grants -in-Aid „salary‟ of ILI by Rs.3.00 crore i.e. Rs.3.00 
crore in BE -2022-23 to Rs.6.00 crore in RE -2022-23. The Department of Legal Affairs has 
provided financial supports as well as administrative support to ILI, whenever they required.  
3.2 ILI has also shared their views on merger of ILI with either the Supreme Court of India 
or the Bar Council of India and stated that the ILI has been functioning effectively under the 
aegis of the Ministry of Law and Justice. ILI has also, therefore, opined that looking to the 
distinct and unique nature and work scope of the Indian Law Institute, it is not viable to merge it 
with either the Supreme Court of India or the Bar Council of India. 
3.3Therefore, it would be appropriate if the ILI continues to maintain its independent existence 
with the financial support of the Department and functions under the aegis of the Ministry of 
Law and Justice. The Department has from time to time accepted mo st of the requests of ILI for 
financial and administrative support.  

 
21 
Further Observation  
3.4 The Committee notes the reply of the Department. Indian Law Institute (ILI) was 
founded in 1956 primarily with the objective of promoting and conducting legal 
research. The Committee observes that either the fund or Grants -in-Aid provided by the 
Department is not sufficient to cater to its basic needs like proper infrastructure, filling up 
of faculty positions and other Academic and Non-Academic activities. The Committee notes 
that even after 60 years of its establishment a premier institute like ILI is struggling to 
cater to meet its essential requirements. The Committee wishes to see ILI as a centre of 
excellence in the field of legal research and therefore strongly recommends the Department 
to increase its allocation. 
VACANCIES OF NOTARIES 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.5 On observing the State/UT-wise sanctioned posts of Notaries it can be observed that their 
distribution is quite uneven. For instance for a much bigger state like Uttar Pradesh the 
sanctioned posts for public notaries is 2650 only, whereas for Gujarat, whic h is a comparatively 
much smaller state in terms of population the strength of notaries is 8000. It is also not known 
what criteria are being used to sanction a particular number of notaries in a State. Accordingly, 
the Committee recommends the Government to use a fair yardstick and take into account the 
factors like population, litigations etc. while sanctioning the posts of Public Notaries in a 
particular State. (3.19) 
Action Taken 
 
3.6 It is submitted that the number of vacancies for Central Government Notaries in the State 
of Uttar Pradesh was inadvertently mentioned as 2650 and the correct figure is 5150, which was 
increased vide Notification G.S.R. 746(E) dated 18th October, 2021. Further, the vacancies in 
the state are increased in accordance with the number of applications received for appointment of 
Notaries for the particular state.  
 
Further observation  
 
3.7 The Committee is of the view that increasing the vacancies in accordance with the 
number of applications received is not a good criterion to decide vacancies for appointment 
of notaries. The Committee desires that the sanctioned strength of notaries in a particular 
state should be determined only on the basis of its population, number of litigation, 
economic and commercial activit ies in that state, etc., and it should  also be reviewed 
regularly.  
 
 
 
 

 
22 
VACANCIES IN THE DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.8 The Panel Counsels are engaged all over the Country by the Central Government to 
conduct litigations before the High Courts/Tribunals and other courts. They bear the major 
burden of litigations against the Central Government. From the submissions made by t he 
Department, it is observed that the fees paid to these counsels are very meagre, which is much 
below the market rates. The last revision of their fees was done about 7 years back. Accordingly, 
the Committee recommends the Department to revise the fees p aid to the panel lawyers suitably, 
considering the current market rates, so that they remain interested and committed in their jobs. 
It will also help in attracting competent lawyers for being empanelled as a panel lawyer for the 
Central Government. (3.23)  
Action Taken 
3.9 Presently there are more than 6000 panel counsels before various Courts across the 
country. The present fee structure to these panel counsel was finalised in year 2015, vide OM 
No. 26(1)/2014/Judl.dated 01.10.2015, which still seems to b e sufficient. As such increase in fee 
structure at this stage does not seem to be required. 
Further observation 
3.10 The Committee  notes the reply. T he fee structure for notaries was  finalised way 
back in the year 2015 and the same fee structure is continuing till date . The Committee 
therefore recommends the Department to revise the fees taking into account the inflation 
rate over the past 8 years.
